events.title: Under the Elm - Next Fest Demo Livestream!
events.summary: Come wander the woods with me - quiet gameplay from the free Under the Elm demo during Steam Next Fest.

events.title: 0.8.4 - Come sit with Gram
events.summary: Just a reminder: The free demo is in Steam Next Fest until October 26, and Under the Elm comes out November 4! Visiting Gram You can sit on Gram's bench in the Memorial Garden now! Her stone sits under the Grandmother Beech, its leaves drift down around you (snow in winter), and the light follows the hour you come - pink at dawn, gold at dusk, dark at night. events.title: Play the Under the Elm demo in Steam Next Fest!
events.summary: Forage real mushrooms and herbs, learn to tell them from their poisonous twins, brew her old recipes, and get to know the village she left behind. The demo covers your first two weeks, and the first signs that the woods have changed since she died. "A peaceful, beautifully grounded nature escape. A true hidden gem!" - Review Score Pollution If you try it, the Feedback button in the pause menu sends your notes to me, and if it's your kind of game, a wishlist helps a lot before launch on November

events.title: The Fair Folk, Part 2 of 4: Old Protections
events.summary: Part 2 of The Fair Folk is out, in the full game and the free demo. The tricks at night are getting bolder, and they reach for more than your basket now. A few people in the village still remember how their grandparents kept a house safe, if you ask the right ones. Keep an eye on the grass after rain. events.title: Update 0.6.0 - The Fair Folk, Part 1 of 4: The First Signs
events.summary: Something has been finding its way out of the woods since she died, and 0.6.0 is where it starts to show. This is the first of four parts of The Fair Folk, the story update I've been building toward. Gabriel has been spending his nights at the window. The village isn't quite itself. And Rowan has something new to teach you, if you bring him the right thing. It picks up from wherever you are - a brand new game, or one you've been playing for weeks. events.title: 0.5.10 - Tools in Hand and a Tidier Shop
events.summary: Tools you can see A new row under your basket shows the tools you've earned - and the shadows of the ones still ahead. Upgrade your axe, pickaxe or knife and the one in your hands changes to match. The "A New Tool" moment now shows the tool itself, with a fuller description. At the bench Make Another repeats the remedy you just made. Lay It Again sets the same page back out. A bottle counter in the corner keeps count as you go. events.title: 0.5.9 - The Oak Forest is in bloom again
events.summary: A player on the Discord went looking for flowers in the Oak Forest and came back empty-handed. It turned out the forest had stopped growing most of its plants - the trees had filled in so thickly that the game couldn't find room for them. That's fixed, and the woods are full of things to pick again, in every season! Also new: A garden quest that could only be finished in spring now works all year round. events.title: A warmer welcome to the valley
events.summary: 0.5.4 - A Warmer Welcome This update rebuilds the first days in the valley. A playtester (thanks Amanda!) told me in no uncertain terms that the quests could have reached her faster at the beginning, and she was right: most of what the village had to teach you was waiting behind letters that arrived days apart, so I rejiggered the beginning spine to make the speed of settling in match any play style. events.title: Update 0.5.3 - The story now has an ending
events.summary: The story now has an ending Under the Elm's main story now has a proper close! Help every villager with their final request, and the cabin has one last thing waiting for you. I won't say more than that - but I will say it's the part of this game I'm proudest of, and it wrecks me every time I play it. The credits are new too! events.title: 0.5.2 - The Lively Village
events.summary: Until now, the village in Under the Elm was pretty quiet. Most folks stayed indoors through the day, and when you walked into town you'd find maybe a few people standing around. It never felt like a place people actually lived. This update (hopefully) changes that! Villagers have schedules now. Wren is out in her garden watering and weeding. events.title: Under the Elm 0.5.0 - The Alchemy Bench, Before and After
events.summary: The alchemy bench used to be a (fairly boring) menu. You'd pick a recipe from a grid, the game would check you had the ingredients, and you'd press Make. It worked, but it meant every remedy was really a shopping list - and knowing what a plant actually does never mattered once you had the list, which isn't exactly what I wanted to bring to you. Not in a game whose whole purpose is to teach!So I've spent the past few weeks rebuilding it - along with everything else a rebuild of this magnitude to

events.title: 0.4.0 - Identification, rebuilt
events.summary: Identification, rebuiltIdentifying used to be one button. You'd bring an unknown mushroom back, press Identify, and the game would tell you what it was. It worked, but it wasn't really foraging - the mushroom in your basket was a lockbox and the button was the key. events.title: A Discord & a Press Kit!
events.summary: Under the Elm now has a Discord and a press kit!The Discord is the studio's home rather than any one game's - small and quiet on purpose. Come tell me what you found in the woods, ask about a mushroom you can't identify, report a bug or just come say hi! https://discord.gg/mcyUrKfNQK The press kit has screenshots, key art, the fact sheet, and blanket permission to record, stream, and monetize any video of the game.
